text: dsh-peak-hours 是面向 DSH Web 的运行时段控制插件。它在 composer 中提供运行模式按钮，并在宿主侧依据北京时间排程，在高峰时段暂停任务、于空闲时段恢复。主要功能包括全天运行或仅空闲时段运行、按会话保存模式、显示节假日与下次切换倒计时，以及在高峰时排队等待。适合希望避开中国工作日高峰运行任务的 DSH 用户；无需 API Key 或外部账号。

dsh-peak-hours adds a composer control for always-on or idle-only operation. Its Beijing-time schedule pauses tasks during weekday peak windows and resumes them afterward. It supports per-session modes, holiday and transition displays, and queued waits. No API key or external account is needed.
想让 DSH 只在电价低的时段运行任务。
工作日白天能不能自动暂停 DSH，到了空闲时间再继续？
帮我按北京时间设置任务运行窗口。
不同会话需要各自选择全天运行或空闲时段运行。
Pause my DSH tasks during weekday peak hours and resume them afterward.
Can I set a per-session schedule for when DSH tasks run?
dsh-peak-hours 的功能「schedule」：按北京时间判断工作日 09:00–12:00、14:00–18:00 为高峰，周末、法定节假日及其他时段为空闲。时钟跨越排程边界时重新计算阶段。
dsh-peak-hours 的功能「mode」：在 composer 控件中选择全天运行或仅空闲时段运行。模式可按会话单独设置；未设置的会话继承默认值。
dsh-peak-hours 的功能「pause」：启用仅空闲时段后，任务在高峰窗口的安全执行边界等待；阶段切为空闲时自动恢复，等待支持取消。
dsh-peak-hours 的功能「display」：界面显示当前北京时间、运行阶段、下次切换、节假日状态及排队任务，并在高峰时提示等待倒计时。
想在法定节假日避免把 DSH 任务误判为工作日高峰。
Let queued work continue automatically when the next idle window begins.

dsh-peak-hours README · dsh-peak-hours：A run-window switch for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

It adds a control to the right of the composer's mode buttons that chooses between **running always** and
**running only in off-peak hours**. In the second mode every dsh task — including one that is already
running — is paused when a peak-price window starts and resumed automatically when it ends.

Available in **English** (this file) and **[中文](README.zh.md)**.

dsh-peak-hours README · Run windows：Off-peak is the half-price window. Peak, in Beijing time (UTC+8), is:

| When | Phase |
| --- | --- |
| Monday–Friday, 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00, excluding Chinese statutory holidays | peak |
| Everything else — 00:00–09:00, 12:00–14:00, 18:00–24:00, all weekend, all statutory holidays | idle |

Make-up workdays (weekends that are worked to offset a holiday) stay **idle**: the rule only looks at the
weekday and whether the date is a statutory holiday.

dsh-peak-hours README · Install：From the dsh CLI:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:lion231226/dsh-peak-hours
```

The plugin is pure JavaScript with no build step and no runtime dependencies, so a source install is enough.

dsh-peak-hours README · Install：For a desktop profile that is currently running, this repository also ships `install.ps1`, which copies the
package into `%DSH_HOME%\profiles\<profile>\node_modules\` and maintains one managed row in the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`. It validates the patch file with js-yaml before writing (a malformed patch file stops the
Loader from reconciling the whole profile), waits for the plugin to answer, and re-activates the entry with a
fresh row id if a previous attempt left it failed. No restart is required.

dsh-peak-hours README · Install：> **Do not mix the two install paths.** `dsh plugin add` registers the package as a profile bundle, and the
> bundle layer then contributes the patch row from the package's own `cordis.patch.yml`. `install.ps1` writes
> that row by hand instead; running it against a profile that already has the bundle would leave two entries
> with the same id, and nothing downstream de-duplicates them (the patch applier pushes inserted rows as-is and
> the cordis Loader has no duplicate check). The script now refuses to run in that case.

dsh-peak-hours README · Install：```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1 -Uninstall
```

dsh-peak-hours README · Using it：The button sits in the composer tool row, immediately to the right of the mode buttons (the permission and
plan selectors). It has three states:

| State | Label | Dot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run always | 全天运行 / Run always | neutral |
| Off-peak only, currently idle | 空闲时段 · 运行中 / Off-peak · running | green |
| Off-peak only, currently peak | 空闲时段 · 已暂停 / Off-peak · paused | amber |

dsh-peak-hours README · Using it：Clicking it opens a panel with the two modes, the current Beijing time, the next switch and a per-second
countdown, today's holiday (when there is one), a warning when the holiday calendar has no data for the year,
and a note while a clock override is active.

While a peak window is in force, a banner above the composer card states that submitted tasks will start
automatically at the end of the window, with a live countdown.

dsh-peak-hours README · How the pause works：1. **`agent/pre-step`** — before every model call. An abort during the wait is re-thrown, which is the control
   flow the agent loop already expects (`signal.throwIfAborted()` follows the waterfall).
2. **`tools/pre-execute`** — before every tool body is dispatched, covering a step that runs into a peak
   window. On abort it returns the runtime's designed `{ kind: 'cancel' }` instead of throwing, because a
   throwing listener is classified as a scheduler failure and fails the whole step.

dsh-peak-hours README · How the pause works：The gate releases immediately when the phase is idle, and while a peak window is in force it registers a
waiter and arms a single timer at the exact next transition instant — no polling, no busy loop. When the timer
fires, the phase is re-evaluated and every waiter is released, so the work continues on its own.

dsh-peak-hours README · How the pause works：`llm/stream` is deliberately not gated: it returns an `AsyncIterable` rather than a promise, and the agent loop
has a call path that bypasses it, so the primary gate already covers every model call.

Nothing is lost while waiting: messages and tool calls stay in the session log, no model request is made, and
the wait is abortable (pressing stop cancels it).

dsh-peak-hours README · HTTP API：Registered on the host's loopback web server; no GUI token is required on loopback.

The mode is **per session**: every session carries its own choice, and a task is judged by the session that
owns it. A session with no explicit choice follows `default`.

dsh-peak-hours README · HTTP API：| Method | Path | Body / result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/peak-hours/health` | `{ ok, plugin, version }` |
| GET | `/api/peak-hours/state?session=<id>` | the state envelope below; without `?session=` it reports `default` |
| POST | `/api/peak-hours/mode` | `{ "mode": "always" \| "idle-only" \| null, "session"?: "<id>", "scope"?: "session" \| "default" }` — `mode: null` with a session clears that override; neither field writes `default`. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` |
| POST | `/api/peak-hours/clock` | `{ "offsetMs": <int\|null>, "ttlMs"?: <int> }`; `ttlMs` is capped at 30 minutes |

dsh-peak-hours README · HTTP API：```jsonc
{ "ok": true, "state": {
  "mode": "always", "defaultMode": "always", "modeSource": "session",
  "sessionId": "session-abc", "phase": "idle", "reason": "off-hours",
  "now": 1791541815888, "nowText": "2026-10-09 18:30:15",

dsh-peak-hours README · HTTP API：`waitingTasks` counts **the session named by `?session=`**, and the whole host when the parameter is absent —
which is why the older session-less curl examples keep their meaning. `waitingTasksTotal` is always host-wide.
`waitingTasksUnresolved` counts waiters whose session could not be resolved; those follow `default`, and the
count exists so a resolution failure is visible instead of looking like "nothing is waiting".

dsh-peak-hours README · HTTP API：`clockOverride` shifts the host's notion of "now" so a peak window can be simulated without waiting for one.
It always carries a TTL (10 minutes by default) and clears itself: without that, a session that is held by the
window it created has nothing left to release it. Set `DSH_PEAK_HOURS_ALLOW_CLOCK=0` to disable the endpoint.

dsh-peak-hours README · Holiday data：The built-in calendar lists every statutory day off in 2025 (28 days) and 2026 (33 days), taken from the
State Council holiday notices. Make-up workdays are not part of the set. Each entry keeps its source titles
and URLs in `HOLIDAY_SOURCE_DETAIL` inside `lib/core/holidays.js`.

dsh-peak-hours README · Holiday data：The 2027 notice has not been published yet, so that year reports `holidayCoverage: "unknown"` with
`unknownHolidayYear: 2027` and treats the date as a non-holiday (a weekday inside a window is peak); the UI
surfaces the warning. Adding a year is one data entry.

Callers can overlay their own dates with `createCalendar({ extra: { '2027-01-01': '元旦' } })`; `extra` wins and
is not restricted by `years`.

dsh-peak-hours README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowClockOverride` | `true` | Whether `POST /api/peak-hours/clock` is accepted |
| `version` | from package.json | Version reported by `/health` |

dsh-peak-hours README · Configuration：Per-session choices live in `%DSH_HOME%\peak-hours-state.json` as
`{ "version": 2, "default": "always", "sessions": { "<sessionId>": "idle-only" } }`, written with serialized
atomic writes. An older `{ "mode": ... }` file is migrated on first read — `default` takes that value and
`sessions` starts empty — and a corrupt file falls back to `always` with an empty table, logging once. The table
is capped at 500 entries and evicts the least recently written one, logging each eviction. Disposing the plugin
releases every listener, timer and route.

dsh-peak-hours README · Known limits：* A model call that has already been issued is not interrupted; the task pauses at its next safe boundary.
* Background processes in a terminal, and background shells started as jobs, are not agent steps and are not
  gated.
* A message submitted during a peak window is not dropped — it waits and continues when the window ends.
* Each session with a mounted client keeps its own poll (15 s, 3 s near a boundary), so request volume grows
  with the number of open sessions.
* Writing `default` changes every session that has no override of its own; the composer states that scope
  before the change is made.

dsh-peak-hours README · Upgrading from 0.1.x：The mode used to be one host-wide value. It now lives per session, and the old value becomes `default`, so
**every session without its own entry keeps behaving exactly as before** after the upgrade. Two things to know:

dsh-peak-hours README · Upgrading from 0.1.x：* **Refresh the window after installing.** A page still running the 0.1.x client sends a bare `{mode}` write,
  which the new host correctly reads as "write `default`" — i.e. the old bundle would reproduce the very bug
  this release fixes.
* **Downgrading loses `sessions`.** An 0.1.x build ignores the `sessions` table and rewrites the file in the old
  shape, so back up or delete `%DSH_HOME%\peak-hours-state.json` before going back.

dsh-peak-hours README · Tests：```sh
node --test                          # author suites + the independent verification suite
node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"     # author suites only
node --test "verify/**/*.test.mjs"   # independent verification only
node tools/smoke-host.mjs            # host half against a fake context, over real HTTP

dsh-peak-hours README · Tests：`test/` holds the author suites (core schedule, host gate/routes/store, client). `verify/` holds an
independent suite written against the same contracts: a day-by-day check of the holiday calendar against the
official notices, a boundary matrix at one-second resolution, property tests over the transition function,
gate semantics under a fake clock, adversarial cases, client bundle checks, and a harness that mounts the
plugin under the real cordis runtime. `verify/EVIDENCE.md` records each command with its raw output.
dsh-peak-hours README · Tests：Node 24 rejects a directory argument for `node --test`, hence the glob patterns above.

dsh-peak-hours README · Field test (real clock, no simulation)：On Monday 2026-10-12, with the plugin in off-peak mode, a message submitted at 09:01:58 Beijing time — inside
the morning peak window — was held for 178 minutes. The session log for that run shows the message entering the
inbox at `09:01:58.530`, the turn opening two milliseconds later, then **no event of any kind** until
`step/start` at `12:00:03.051` — three seconds after the boundary at 12:00:00 — followed by the model request at
`12:00:03.054`. Nothing was dropped and no interval was skipped: the work simply waited for the window to end.
